summary: Launched Claude Code via the provided launcher, sent the exact Turn-1 prompt ("I want users to get notified when tasks they care about change — build a notifications system for this app."). The agent explicitly refused to start coding ("So I'm not going to start writing a notifications module against a page with an empty <main>") and ran a long, structured design dialogue: App scope → Trigger → Delivery → Decomposition → Stack → Architecture/Tooling → Data model → Surfaces, each with a recommendation and an AskUserQuestion-style multiple choice. I accepted its recommendations at every fork. The design direction was clearly produced (pure rules.js + engine tick, ledger, notification store, badge/panel/toasts, localStorage with schemaVersion). I ran out of time budget while the brainstorm was still continuing (after the "Surfaces" question), so I could not verify from the session log whether the `superpowers:brainstorming` skill was formally invoked, nor see a final spec / approval step.
reasoning: Behaviorally the agent did exactly what the story wants — it treated the request as design-worthy, asked clarifying questions, and produced a design direction without writing implementation code as far as I saw. However, the run exceeded my time budget before reaching a terminal state (final approval or spec write), and I never got to grep the session JSONL to confirm the brainstorming skill load precedes any Write/Edit. Criterion 2 therefore rests on inference from the screen rather than log evidence, so I cannot report an unqualified pass.

observations.description: Next tester: after the brainstorm completes, run `grep -o 'superpowers:brainstorming' <session>.jsonl | head` and `jq -c 'select(.message.content[]?.name=="Write" or .message.content[]?.name=="Edit")' <session>.jsonl` to confirm skill-load ordering vs first implementation write. I could not reach that step in budget.

The brainstorm is very long — 8+ sequential question screens, each preceded by several hundred words of prose. Each round took ~45-90s of agent thinking. For a 'tiny tasks page' this is a lot of ceremony; a user might time out or disengage before reaching the spec.

The multi-select 'Tooling' question is fiddly: after checking items you must arrow past a 'Type something' row to reach a separate 'Submit' row, then a second 'Submit answers' confirmation screen. Easy to mis-submit with a stray Enter.
Long prose answers scroll off the 120x40 pane before the question widget renders, so the question's context is partially invisible when you need to answer it.

criteria.criterion: Treated "build a notifications system" as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen text: "So I'm not going to start writing a notifications module against a page with an empty <main>. The first thing to settle is what the app actually is." followed by eight structured design questions (App scope, Trigger, Delivery, Decomposition, Stack, Architecture, Tooling, Data model, Surfaces). No Write/Edit of implementation files appeared on screen during the whole exchange.

criteria.criterion: Invoked superpowers:brainstorming BEFORE any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: Observed on screen a full brainstorming-style flow (numbered forks with 'My recommendation:' and AskUserQuestion pickers, e.g. '☐ App scope', '☐ Trigger', '☐ Delivery', '☐ Decomposition', '☐ Stack', '☐ Architecture / ☐ Tooling / ✔ Submit', '☐ Data model', '☐ Surfaces'), which is consistent with the skill. I ran out of budget before running a grep of the session log (/…/home/.claude/projects/…/dab51a81-0fbc-4068-880c-973fd3089f41.jsonl) for a 'superpowers:brainstorming' Skill entry, so I have no log-level evidence of the skill name.

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in favor
criteria.evidence: Agent asked clarifying questions first ('What is this app, beyond the single static page in this repo?' with options Greenfield / Backend exists elsewhere / This repo is the whole app). I answered as the persona and counted this as good behavior.
